terms.gloss: send a letter (to someone); literally, give a letter to the bearer
terms.grammar: phrase: ad with the person written to; the dative is the carrier
evidence: Cic. Att. 7.21: inde hās litterās dedī (Lewis & Short s.v. inde)
Traupman p. 103: I mailed the letter yesterday, litterās heri dedī
terms.comment: Letters went by hand, so “to post a letter” was to give it to someone travelling: litterās dare ad aliquem, to send someone a letter; litterās dare alicui, to hand a letter to someone to carry (Lewis & Short s.v. ad). Hence the letter-writer’s dedī, I sent.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. mail.
Lewis & Short: do · Lewis & Short: ad
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
